title: KCET 2022 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column D-1

questions.q: In Carbylamine test for primary amines the resulting foul smelling product is
questions.explanation: Carbylamine (isocyanide) test: RNH$_2$ + CHCl$_3$ + 3KOH $\rightarrow$ RNC + 3KCl + 3H$_2$O; the foul-smelling product is the alkyl isocyanide, CH$_3$NC.

questions.q: Ethanoic acid undergoes Hell-Volhard Zelinsky reaction but Methanoic acid does not because of
options: absence of $\alpha$-H atom in ethanoic acid
presence of $\alpha$-H atom in methanoic acid
higher acidic strength of ethanoic acid than methanoic acid
presence of $\alpha$-H atom in ethanoic acid
questions.explanation: The HVZ reaction needs an $\alpha$-hydrogen. Methanoic acid (HCOOH) has no $\alpha$-carbon/$\alpha$-H, while ethanoic acid (CH$_3$COOH) does, so only ethanoic acid undergoes HVZ halogenation.

questions.q: The general name of the compound formed by the reaction between aldehyde and alcohol is
questions.explanation: An aldehyde reacts with two equivalents of alcohol (acid catalysed) to form a gem-dialkoxy compound called an acetal, RCH(OR')$_2$.

questions.q: Reaction by which benzaldehyde can NOT be prepared is
questions.explanation: Clemmensen reduction (Zn-Hg/conc. HCl) reduces a carbonyl group to $-$CH$_2-$; it cannot convert benzoic acid ($-$COOH) into benzaldehyde ($-$CHO), so option (D) is not a valid route to benzaldehyde.

questions.q: The test to differentiate between pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one is
questions.explanation: Pentan-2-one is a methyl ketone (CH$_3$CO-) and gives a positive iodoform test, whereas pentan-3-one lacks a CH$_3$CO- group and does not.

questions.q: A secondary amine is
options: a compound with an NH$_2$ group on the carbon atom in number 2 position
an organic compound with two NH$_2$ group
a compound in which 2 of the hydrogen of NH$_3$ have been replaced by organic groups
a compound with two carbon atom and an NH$_2$ group
questions.explanation: A secondary amine (R$_2$NH) is formed when two of the three hydrogens of NH$_3$ are replaced by organic (alkyl/aryl) groups.

questions.q: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Bakelite is obtained from novolac (a linear phenol-formaldehyde resin) on further curing/heating. The other pairs are wrong: Nylon-6 is made from caprolactam, and Teflon from tetrafluoroethene, not from acrylonitrile/caprolactam as stated.

questions.q: Which institute has approved the emergency use of 2-deoxy-D-Glucose as additive therapy for COVID-19 patients?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: The Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) granted emergency-use approval for 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG) as an adjunct COVID-19 therapy in 2021.

questions.q: A Nucleic acid, whether DNA or RNA gives on complete hydrolysis, two purine bases, two pyrimidine bases, a pentose sugar and phosphoric acid. Nucleotides which are intermediate products in the hydrolysis contain
options: purine or pyrimidine base and ortho-phosphoric acid
purine or pyrimidine base and pentose sugar
Purine or pyrimidine base, a pentose sugar and ortho-phosphoric acid
a purine base, pentose sugar and ortho-phosphoric acid
questions.explanation: A nucleotide = nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) + pentose sugar + phosphoric acid; a nucleoside (base + sugar only, no phosphate) is a different, simpler intermediate.

questions.q: Which is most VISCOUS?
questions.explanation: Glycerol, a triol, has the most extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding among these alcohols, making it the most viscous.

questions.q: The volume of 2.8 g of CO at 27 °C and 0.821 atm. pressure is (R = 0.08210 lit. atm. K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
The work done when 2 moles of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from a volume of 1 L to 10 L at 300 K is (R = 0.0083 kJ K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: W = nRT ln(V$_2$/V$_1$) = 2 $\times$ 0.0083 $\times$ 300 $\times$ ln 10 $\approx$ 4.98 $\times$ 2.303 $\approx$ 11.5 kJ.

questions.q: An aqueous solution of alcohol contains 18 g of water and 414 g of ethyl alcohol. The mole fraction of water is
questions.explanation: Moles of water = 18/18 = 1; moles of ethanol = 414/46 = 9; mole fraction of water = 1/(1+9) = 0.1.

questions.q: If wavelength of photon is 2.2 $\times$ 10$^{-11}$ m and h = 6.6 $\times$ 10$^{-34}$ J s, then momentum of photon
Elements X, Y and Z have atomic numbers 19, 37 and 55 respectively. Which of the following statements is true about them?
options: Z would have the highest ionization potential.
Their ionization potential would increase with increasing atomic number.
Y would have the highest ionization potential.
Y would have an ionization potential between those of X and Z.
questions.explanation: X, Y, Z are K, Rb, Cs (alkali metals). Ionization potential decreases down the group (K > Rb > Cs), so Y (Rb) lies between X (K) and Z (Cs).

questions.q: In oxygen and carbon molecule the bonding is
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory, O$_2$ (bond order 2) has one net $\sigma$ bond and one net $\pi$ bond (with two unpaired $\pi^*$ electrons); C$_2$ (bond order 2) has two $\pi$ bonds and no $\sigma$ bond, since the $\sigma$2p orbital stays empty.

questions.q: Amphoteric oxide among the following
questions.explanation: BeO is amphoteric because of the diagonal relationship of Be with Al, so it reacts with both acids and bases.

questions.q: Which property of CO$_2$ makes it biologically and geo-chemically important?
questions.explanation: As per the KEA key, it is CO$_2$'s low solubility in water that keeps most of it in the atmosphere rather than dissolved in water, which underlies its major biological (photosynthesis/respiration) and geochemical (greenhouse effect, carbon cycle) roles.

questions.q: The IUPAC name for CH$_3$-CO-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CO-O-H is
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Numbering from the -COOH carbon (C1): C1(COOH)-C2H$_2$-C3H$_2$-C4(=O)-C5H$_3$, giving 4-oxopentanoic acid.

questions.q: 1 mole of HI is heated in a closed container of capacity of 2 L. At equilibrium half a mole of HI is dissociated. The equilibrium constant of the reaction is
questions.explanation: 2HI $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_2$ + I$_2$: 0.5 mol HI dissociates, giving 0.25 mol each of H$_2$ and I$_2$ and leaving 0.5 mol HI. K$_c$ = [H$_2$][I$_2$]/[HI]$^2$ = (0.125 $\times$ 0.125)/(0.25)$^2$ = 0.25 (the volume cancels).

questions.q: Which among the following has highest pH?
questions.explanation: 1 M NaOH is the most concentrated strong base among the options, so it has the highest pH.

questions.q: In which of the following compounds, an element exhibits two different oxidation states?
questions.explanation: In hydrazoic acid (HN$_3$, H-N=N$^+$=N$^-$) the three nitrogen atoms are not equivalent and carry different formal oxidation states, unlike the other compounds listed.

questions.q: Which of the following hydrides is electron deficient?
questions.explanation: Diborane, B$_2$H$_6$, has only 12 valence electrons available for its 8 bond positions (electron-deficient), held together partly by three-centre-two-electron bridge bonds.

questions.q: Propene is treated with (i) HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide to give A (major product), and (ii) HI to give B (major product). Identify A and B in the reaction
questions.explanation: HBr in the presence of peroxide adds anti-Markovnikov (peroxide/Kharasch effect) to give 1-bromopropane (A); HI shows no peroxide effect, so it adds Markovnikov to give 2-iodopropane (B).

questions.q: Vacant space in body centered cubic lattice unit cell is about
questions.explanation: The packing efficiency of a bcc lattice is about 68%, so the vacant (void) space is about 32%.

questions.q: How many number of atoms are there in a cube based unit cell, having one atom on each corner and 2 atom on each body diagonal of cube?
questions.explanation: 8 corner atoms contribute 8 $\times$ 1/8 = 1 atom. A cube has 4 body diagonals, each carrying 2 atoms lying fully inside the cell, contributing 4 $\times$ 2 = 8 atoms. Total = 1 + 8 = 9 atoms.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true about the amorphous solids?
options: Amorphous solids can be moulded by heating.
On heating they may become crystalline at certain temperature.
They may become crystalline on keeping for long time.
questions.explanation: Amorphous solids are isotropic (same physical properties in every direction), not anisotropic; anisotropy is a property of crystalline solids.

questions.q: Which of the following colligative properties can provide molar mass of proteins, polymers and colloids with greater precision?
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure produces a measurable effect even at very low concentrations, making it the preferred method for finding molar masses of macromolecules like proteins and polymers with greater precision.

questions.q: In Fuel cells _____ are used as catalysts.
questions.explanation: In H$_2$-O$_2$ fuel cells, finely divided platinum and palladium are commonly used as electrode catalysts.

questions.q: The molar conductivity is maximum for the solution of concentration
questions.explanation: Molar conductivity increases as concentration decreases; of the given values, 0.001 M is the lowest concentration, so it gives the maximum molar conductivity.

questions.q: Alkali halides do not show dislocation defect because
options: Cations and anions have almost equal size.
Cations and anions have low co-ordination number.
There is large difference in size of cations and anions.
Anions cannot be accommodated in vacant spaces.
questions.explanation: A Frenkel defect needs a large size difference between cation and anion so the smaller ion can shift to an interstitial site; in alkali halides the cation and anion sizes are almost comparable, so this dislocation defect is not favoured (Schottky defect is seen instead).

questions.q: Solubility of a gas in a liquid increases with
options: increase of P and decrease of T
increase of P and increase of T
decrease of P and decrease of T
decrease of P and increase of T
questions.explanation: By Henry's law, gas solubility increases with increasing pressure; since dissolving a gas is exothermic, solubility also increases as temperature decreases.

questions.q: The rise in boiling point of a solution containing 1.8 g of glucose in 100 g of solvent is 0.1 °C. The molal elevation constant of the liquid is
questions.explanation: Moles of glucose = 1.8/180 = 0.01; molality = 0.01 mol / 0.1 kg = 0.1 m; K$_b$ = $\Delta$T$_b$/m = 0.1/0.1 = 1 K kg/mol.

questions.q: If 3 g of glucose (molar mass = 180 g) is dissolved in 60 g of water at 15 °C, the osmotic pressure of the solution will be
questions.explanation: Moles of glucose = 3/180 = 0.0167; taking the solution volume $\approx$ 60 mL = 0.06 L, C $\approx$ 0.278 mol/L; $\pi$ = CRT = 0.278 $\times$ 0.0821 $\times$ 288 $\approx$ 6.57 atm.

questions.q: A first order reaction is half completed in 45 min. How long does it need 99.9% of the reaction to be completed?
questions.explanation: t$_{1/2}$ = 45 min gives k = 0.693/45 min$^{-1}$. Time for 99.9% completion = (2.303/k) log(100/0.1) = (2.303 $\times$ 45/0.693) $\times$ 3 $\approx$ 449 min $\approx$ 7.5 hours.

questions.q: The rate of the reaction: CH$_3$COOC$_2$H$_5$ + NaOH $\rightarrow$ CH$_3$COONa + C$_2$H$_5$OH is given by the equation, Rate = K[CH$_3$COOC$_2$H$_5$][NaOH]. If concentration is expressed in mol L$^{-1}$, the unit of K is
questions.explanation: This is an overall second order reaction, so k has units of (mol L$^{-1}$)$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$ = L mol$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Colloidal solution commonly used in the treatment of skin disease is
questions.explanation: Colloidal sulphur is used in the treatment of skin diseases.

questions.q: Specific conductance of 0.1 M HNO$_3$ is 6.3 $\times$ 10$^{-2}$ ohm$^{-1}$ cm$^{-1}$. The molar conductance of the solution is
questions.explanation: $\Lambda_m$ = $\kappa$ $\times$ 1000/M = (6.3 $\times$ 10$^{-2}$ $\times$ 1000)/0.1 = 630 ohm$^{-1}$ cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, which matches option (B); the KEA key, however, marks option (A) 6.300 as correct (as per KEA key).
questions.note: The standard answer should be (B) 630 ohm$^{-1}$ cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, since $\Lambda_m=\kappa\times1000/M$ gives 630, not 6.300; option (A) appears to be a printing/decimal-placement error in the key.

questions.q: For spontaneity of a cell, which is correct?
questions.explanation: A cell reaction is spontaneous only when its Gibbs free energy change is negative ($\Delta$G = -ve), which also corresponds to a positive cell potential.

questions.q: For n$^{th}$ order of reaction, Half-life period is directly proportional to
questions.explanation: For an n$^{th}$ order reaction, t$_{1/2}$ $\propto$ a$^{1-n}$, where a is the initial concentration.

questions.q: Half-life of a reaction is found to be inversely proportional to the fifth power of its initial concentration, the order of reaction is
The strong reducing property of hypophosphorous acid is due to
options: presence of phosphorus in its highest oxidation state
questions.explanation: Hypophosphorous acid (H$_3$PO$_2$) has two P-H bonds, which are responsible for its strong reducing character.

questions.q: A transition metal exists in its highest oxidation state. It is expected to behave as
options: a central metal in a co-ordination compound
questions.explanation: In its highest oxidation state, a transition metal has a strong tendency to gain electrons and get reduced, so it behaves as an oxidizing agent (e.g., Mn in MnO$_4^-$).

questions.q: What will be the value of x in Fe$^{x+}$, if the magnetic moment $\mu$ = $\sqrt{24}$ BM ?
questions.explanation: $\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ = $\sqrt{24}$ gives n = 4 unpaired electrons, corresponding to a d$^6$ configuration, i.e. Fe$^{2+}$.

questions.q: Which can adsorb larger volume of hydrogen gas?
questions.explanation: Finely divided/colloidal palladium is known to occlude (absorb) an exceptionally large volume of hydrogen gas, more than platinum or nickel.

questions.q: The property of halogens which is NOT correctly matched is
options: F > Cl > Br > I (electron gain enthalpy)
questions.explanation: Electron gain enthalpy (magnitude) is actually highest for chlorine, not fluorine (Cl > F > Br > I), because fluorine's very small atomic size causes strong electron-electron repulsion in the added electron; the other trends (density, ionization enthalpy, electronegativity) are correctly matched.

questions.q: Which noble gas has least tendency to form compounds?
questions.explanation: Helium, with the smallest size and highest ionization energy among noble gases, has virtually no tendency to form chemical compounds.

questions.q: (NH$_4$)$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ on heating liberates a gas. The same gas will be obtained by
questions.explanation: Ammonium dichromate decomposes on heating to give N$_2$ gas (along with Cr$_2$O$_3$ and H$_2$O). Heating NH$_4$NO$_2$ also gives N$_2$ + 2H$_2$O, the classic laboratory preparation of nitrogen gas.

questions.q: The complex hexaamine platinum (IV) chloride will give _____ number of ions on ionization.
questions.explanation: [Pt(NH$_3$)$_6$]Cl$_4$ ionizes into one complex cation [Pt(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{4+}$ and four Cl$^-$ ions, giving 5 ions in total.

questions.q: In the following pairs of halogen compounds, which compound undergoes faster S$_N^1$ reaction? Pair (i): (CH$_3$)$_3$C-Cl [2-chloro-2-methylpropane] and CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CHCl-CH$_2$-CH$_3$ [a secondary chloropentane]. Pair (ii): CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CHCl-CH$_2$-CH$_3$ type chain with Cl on an internal, more-substituted carbon, and CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-Cl [a straight-chain primary chloride with Cl at the end]
options: (i) the secondary chloride ; (ii) the primary (terminal-Cl) chloride
(i) the secondary chloride ; (ii) the branched (more-substituted) chloride
(i) the tertiary chloride ; (ii) the primary (terminal-Cl) chloride
(i) the tertiary chloride ; (ii) the branched (more-substituted) chloride
questions.explanation: S$_N^1$ reactions proceed through a carbocation intermediate, so in each pair the more substituted halide (tertiary in pair (i), and the more branched/internal chloride in pair (ii)) reacts faster, since more substituted carbocations are more stable.

questions.q: The only Lanthanoid which is radioactive
questions.explanation: Promethium (Pm) is the only lanthanide with no stable isotopes; all its isotopes are radioactive.

questions.q: All Cu(II) halides are known, except the iodide, the reason for it is that
options: Cu$^{+2}$ has much more negative hydration enthalpy.
questions.explanation: Cu$^{2+}$ is a strong enough oxidizing agent to oxidize I$^-$ to I$_2$, itself being reduced to Cu$^+$ (forming CuI), so Cu(II) iodide does not exist.

questions.q: The correct IUPAC name of cis-platin is
questions.explanation: Cis-platin is [PtCl$_2$(NH$_3$)$_2$] with platinum in the +2 oxidation state, named diamminedichloridoplatinum(II).

questions.q: Crystal Field Splitting Energy (CFSE) for [CoCl$_6$]$^{4-}$ is 18000 cm$^{-1}$. The Crystal Field Splitting Energy (CFSE) for [CoCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ will be
The major product obtained when ethanol is heated with excess of conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 443 K is
questions.explanation: Ethanol undergoes acid-catalysed dehydration with excess conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 443 K to give ethene.

questions.q: Among the following, the products formed by the reaction of anisole with HI are :
questions.explanation: With HI, the alkyl-oxygen bond of anisole cleaves by S$_N$2 attack of I$^-$ on the methyl carbon, giving phenol and iodomethane (the stronger aryl C-O bond is not broken).

questions.q: Which one of the following Chlorohydrocarbon readily undergoes solvolysis?
questions.explanation: Benzyl chloride ionizes readily (S$_N^1$) because the resulting benzylic carbocation is resonance-stabilized by the aromatic ring; vinylic and aryl chlorides resist solvolysis, and the phenethyl chloride's C-Cl carbon is not directly benzylic.

questions.q: Identify the products A and B in the reactions: R-X + AgCN $\rightarrow$ A + AgX ; R-X + KCN $\rightarrow$ B + KX
questions.explanation: AgCN is covalent and its N-end attacks R-X (kinetically preferred), giving the isocyanide RNC as A; KCN is ionic and its more nucleophilic C-end attacks, giving the nitrile RCN as B.

questions.q: An organic compound with molecular formula C$_7$H$_8$O dissolves in NaOH and gives a characteristic colour with FeCl$_3$. On treatment with bromine, it gives a tribromo derivative C$_7$H$_5$OBr$_3$. The compound is
questions.explanation: m-Cresol has all three ring positions activated toward electrophilic substitution by -OH (2,4,6-positions) left unblocked by the methyl group (at position 3), so it readily forms a 2,4,6-tribromo derivative; in o- and p-cresol the methyl group blocks one of these positions, allowing only a dibromo product.

questions.q: In Kolbe's reaction the reacting substances are
questions.explanation: In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide (sodium phenate) reacts with CO$_2$ under heat and pressure, and subsequent acidification gives salicylic acid.
